discovery: The theory of cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmic structure
motivation: Guth proposed that a brief epoch of accelerated expansion explains the flatness, horizon and monopole problems of the hot Big Bang. Linde made the idea workable through new and chaotic inflation, the framework in which nearly all modern models are built. Mukhanov (with the late Chibisov) showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed galaxies and CMB anisotropies, predicting a nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic, Gaussian spectrum with a slight red tilt. Over three decades, COBE, WMAP, Planck, ACT and SPT have confirmed these predictions with great precision: spatial flatness, coherent acoustic peaks, superhorizon correlations in temperature-polarization, Gaussianity, and a spectral index n_s ≈ 0.965, measurably below one, as anticipated. Inflation turned speculation about the first instant into a predictive, quantitative science, and it motivates today's searches for primordial B-mode polarization. It is the cornerstone of modern cosmology.
